newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to spin off scheduled services - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to spin off scheduled services - paper.

text.p: German national carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG plans to spin off its entire scheduled passenger services business and place it into a subsidiary company, the German weekly newspaper Die Woche reported.
Citing a confidential management document, the paper said the new company, to be called Passage AG, would be run by Fred Reid, the executive manager currently in charge of passenger services.

Lufthansa had originally planned to form a fully autonomous passenger services unit and a holding company but this was blocked by the German Federal Aviation Authority, the paper said. That is why Lufthansa's group management board would remain as management board in charge of scheduled passenger services.
Lufthansa was not immediately available for comment.
Die Woche made the article available ahead of publication in Thursday's editions.
